commits.message:
feat(resume-builder): wire Feedback's AI Analysis to real feedback/analyze

CORE already had a real /resume-intelligence/feedback/analyze route
(built during the earlier "hermes-core-integration" merge) that
nothing on the frontend called yet. Checked the schemas before writing
any code: Hermes's HermesResumeFeedbackItem
(title/current/suggested_improvement/why_it_matters/severity/category)
maps almost field-for-field onto the FE's existing FeedbackItem type
(title/currentText/suggestedText/whyItMatters/severity/issueType) --
this screen was clearly designed against this exact capability, it
just never got connected.

ConsultantFeedbackView.tsx: runs a real analysis on mount using the
resume's actual text, replacing the 4 hardcoded "ai_analysis" mock
items with whatever Hermes actually returns. "Apply Suggestion" now
writes the real suggested text into the resume's summary when the
feedback item is summary-related (via a new onApplySummarySuggestion
callback from ConsultantResumeBuilder); for other sections it shows an
honest "update this section manually" note instead of a no-op, since
automatically rewriting skills/experience/education from a feedback
item isn't safely generic the way summary replacement is.

Dropped the 3 mock items sourced from "tech_recruiter", "bench_sales",
and "service_provider" -- there's no comment-thread or marketplace
backend behind any of them (a real recruiter leaving feedback on a
specific consultant's resume needs a persistence + notification layer
that doesn't exist yet), so showing fabricated recruiter feedback next
to real AI feedback would blur which one is genuine. The tab/filter
UI for those sources stays in place for when that capability exists;
"Add Feedback" (a human manually typing in a note during this session)
and "Endorse Skills" are untouched -- they're real local actions, just
not yet persisted anywhere, which is a different, smaller gap than
fabricated content.

New in resume-intelligence.ts: analyzeResumeFeedback(), typed against
Hermes's live HermesResumeFeedbackItem schema (not guessed).

Verified locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean. Browser pass against the mock
server (extended with a feedback/analyze handler returning two
distinct items, one summary-related and one skills-related) --
confirmed the real request fired on mount, both items rendered with
their real title/section/severity/suggestion text, and clicking
"Apply Suggestion" on the summary item actually overwrote the resume's
Professional Summary with the exact suggested text.
